solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply the outer and inner pairs.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply the brackets out term by term and then simplify.

whyThisWorks.value: Multiplying two linear expressions produces a quadratic because the highest-power product is x × x = x². The two cross-products both contain a single x, so they are like terms and merge into one. That structure — square term, sum term, product term — holds for every expansion of this shape.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading 2 × 8 as 10 and writing the constant as 10.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dropping the x² term when writing the answer in order.

examTip.value: Write the answer in descending powers of x every time: x² term, x term, then the number. Examiners expect that order and it makes checking easier.
